title.zh: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝
title.raw: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝 Volume 7 Annals 7: Emperor Fei I

sentences.zh: 前廢帝諱子業，小字法師，孝武帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor's taboo name was Ziye; his childhood name was Fashi. He was the eldest son of Emperor Xiao Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei I was named Ziye; his childhood name was Fashi. He was Emperor Xiao Wu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年正月甲申生。

translations.literal: He was born on jiashen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on jiashen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，子業留京邑。

translations.literal: When Shizu garrisoned Xunyang, Ziye remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Emperor Xiao Wu held Xunyang, Ziye stayed behind in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十年，世祖入伐元凶，被囚侍中下省，將見害者數矣，卒得無恙。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Shizu entered the capital to attack the prime culprit, he was imprisoned in the Central Secretariat sub-bureau of the palace attendants' office; he was several times on the point of being killed, yet in the end came to no harm.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when the emperor marched in to punish the assassin prince, Ziye was held prisoner in the attendants' sub-bureau; more than once he was nearly executed, yet in the end escaped unharmed.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiao Wu succeeded, Ziye was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始未之東宮，中庶子、二率並入直永福省。

translations.literal: At first he had not yet gone to the Eastern Palace; the crown prince's tutors and the two commandants all entered duty at Yongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had not yet moved into the Eastern Palace, so his tutors and the two palace guard commandants all took up duty at Yongfu Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，出居東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he took up residence in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: [1]四年，講孝經於崇正殿。

translations.literal: [1] In the fourth year, the Classic of Filial Piety was lectured upon in Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: [1] In the fourth year he heard lectures on the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 七年，加元服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he received the cap of adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he underwent the coming-of-age ceremony.

sentences.zh: 八年閏五月庚申，世祖崩，其日，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year, on gengshen day, Shizu died; on that same day the crown prince took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year Emperor Xiao Wu died, and the crown prince succeeded that same day.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭解尚書令，加中書監，驃騎大將軍柳元景加尚書令。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, was relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing and given the additional post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was given the additional post of Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, stepped down as Director of the Masters of Writing and was named Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 甲子，置錄尚書，太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On jiazi day the Recorder of the Masters of Writing was established; Grand Preceptor the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, was made Recorder of Masters of Writing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the post of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was created, and Grand Preceptor Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, was made Recorder of Masters of Writing Affairs.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍柳元景加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was given the additional title of Grand Master with the Golden Ax and Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Ziren, Prince of Yongjia, Administrator of Danyang, was made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziren, Prince of Yongjia and Administrator of Danyang, was appointed Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

translations.literal: [2] (Editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: [2] (End of note.)

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，詔曰：「朕以眇身，夙紹洪業，敬御天威，欽對靈命。

translations.literal: On xinwei day in the sixth month an edict declared: "With my slight person I have long since inherited the great enterprise, reverently wielding Heaven's majesty and respectfully facing the numinous mandate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day in the sixth month an edict declared: "Though my person is slight, I have long since inherited the great enterprise, reverently wielding Heaven's majesty and facing the sacred mandate with awe.

sentences.zh: 仰遵凝緒，日鑒前圖，實可以拱默守成，詒風長世。

translations.literal: Looking up to follow the settled order and daily taking former models as my mirror, I could in truth fold my hands in silence and preserve what has been achieved, passing down good customs to distant ages.
translations.idiomatic: Following the settled order of my forebears and taking past models as my daily guide, I might truly have folded my hands in silence, guarded what was already won, and let good customs endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 而寶位告始，萬宇改屬，惟德弗明，昧于大道。

translations.literal: Yet as the precious throne is only now announced and the myriad realms have changed their allegiance, my virtue is not yet clear and I am still obscure to the Great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne has only just been announced and the realm has only just changed hands; my virtue is not yet clear, and I am still blind to the Great Way.

sentences.zh: 思宣睿範，引茲簡恤，可具詢執事，詳訪民隱。

translations.literal: I wish to proclaim a wise standard and extend this simple compassion; let all responsible officials be consulted in full and the people's hidden hardships investigated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to proclaim a wise standard and extend this simple compassion—let every responsible office be consulted and the people's hidden hardships investigated in detail.

sentences.zh: 凡曲令密文，繁而傷治，[3]關市僦稅，事施一時，而姦吏舞文，妄興威福，加以氣緯舛互，[4]偏頗滋甚。

translations.literal: As for tortuous ordinances and secret statutes, burdensome and harmful to good government, [3] market tolls and lease taxes imposed for a single occasion, while corrupt clerks manipulate the written law and presumptuously wield authority and favor, and moreover the qi and celestial markers are at cross purposes, [4] partiality and excess grow ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Tortuous ordinances and secret statutes burden government; [3] market tolls and lease taxes meant for a moment's need are twisted by corrupt clerks who manipulate the written law and wield power arbitrarily, while the qi and celestial signs fall out of alignment [4] and bias and excess grow worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 宜其寬傜輕憲，以救民切。

translations.literal: Corvée and punishments should be relaxed and lightened to meet the people's urgent needs.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée and punishments should be eased and lightened to relieve the people's urgent distress.

sentences.zh: 御府諸署，事不須廣，雕文篆刻，無施於今。

translations.literal: The various offices of the imperial household need not be broad; carved inscriptions and seal-cut ornament have no place in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices of the imperial household need not be numerous; carved inscriptions and seal-cut ornament have no place today.

sentences.zh: 悉宜并省，以酬氓願。

translations.literal: All alike should be merged and reduced, to answer the common people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: All alike should be merged and cut back, to answer the people's wishes.

sentences.zh: 藩王貿貨，壹皆禁斷。

translations.literal: Princes' trade in goods is entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Princely trade in goods is forbidden altogether.

sentences.zh: 外便具條以聞。

translations.literal: Outside the capital let detailed lists be prepared and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital, let detailed lists be prepared and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」戊寅，以豫州之淮南郡復為南梁郡，復分宣城還置淮南郡。

translations.literal: " On wuyin day Huainan Commandery in Yuzhou was restored as Nanliang Commandery, and Xuancheng was again separated out to re-establish Huainan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " On wuyin day Huainan Commandery in Yuzhou was restored as Nanliang Commandery, and Xuancheng was split off again to re-establish Huainan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以南海太守袁曇遠為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengchen day Yuan Tanyuan, Administrator of Nanhai, was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Yuan Tanyuan, Administrator of Nanhai, was appointed Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史晉安王子勛改為江州刺史，中護軍宗慤為安西將軍、雍州刺史，鎮北將軍、徐州刺史湘東王彧為護軍將軍，中軍將軍義陽王昶為征北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On jihai day in the seventh month of autumn, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou Liu Zixun, Prince of Jin'an, was changed to Inspector of Jiangzhou; Central Army Guard Zong Que was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, was made General Who Protects the Army; General of the Central Army Liu Chang, Prince of Yiyang, was made General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the seventh month of autumn, Liu Zixun, Prince of Jin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, was reassigned as Inspector of Jiangzhou; Central Army Guard Zong Que became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou, became General Who Protects the Army; and Liu Chang, Prince of Yiyang, General of the Central Army, became General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，婆皇國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On gengxu day the state of Pohuang sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day the state of Pohuang sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 崇皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The Honored Empress Dowager was elevated to Grand Empress Dowager, and the empress to Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Honored Empress Dowager was elevated to Grand Empress Dowager, and the empress to Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，罷南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On yimao day the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來所改制度，還依元嘉。

translations.literal: The institutions changed since Xiaojian were restored to follow Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions changed since the Xiaojian era were restored to the Yuanjia standard.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，追崇獻妃為獻皇后。

translations.literal: On bingchen day the late Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day the late Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞解領司徒。

translations.literal: On yichou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 八月丁卯，領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingmao day in the eighth month, General Who Protects the Army Wang Xuamo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day in the eighth month, General Who Protects the Army Wang Xuamo was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: [5]己巳，以青、冀二州刺史蕭惠開為益州刺史。

translations.literal: [5] On jisi day Xiao Hui Kai, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: [5] On jisi day Xiao Hui Kai, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，[6]皇太后崩。

translations.literal: On jichou day [6] the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day [6] the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 京師雨水。

translations.literal: In the capital region rain fell for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rain fell in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，[7]遣御史與官長隨宜賑卹。

translations.literal: On gengyin day [7] censors were dispatched together with office heads to give relief as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day [7] censors were sent out with office heads to give relief wherever it was needed.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，護軍將軍湘東王彧為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On xinchou day in the ninth month, Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Protects the Army in chief.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day in the ninth month, Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army, was made chief General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以尚書左僕射劉遵考為特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On guimao day Liu Zunkao, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Special Advance and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Liu Zunkao, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was promoted to Special Advance and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，文穆皇后祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: On yimao day Empress Wenmu was enshrined beside the Jingning tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Empress Wenmu was enshrined at the Jingning tomb.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲戌，太常建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day in the tenth month of winter, Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, Minister of Ceremonies, was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day in the tenth month of winter, Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an and Minister of Ceremonies, was appointed General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin day Zong Yue, General Who Assists the State, was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Zong Yue, General Who Assists the State, was appointed Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: [8]庚辰，原除揚、南徐州大明七年逋租。

translations.literal: [8] On gengchen day overdue rents from the seventh year of Daming in Yang and Southern Xuzhou were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: [8] On gengchen day overdue rents from the seventh year of Daming in Yang and Southern Xuzhou were remitted.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On yiyou day in the twelfth month, Yan Shibo, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the twelfth month, Yan Shibo, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was confirmed as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: [9]壬辰，以王畿諸郡為揚州，以揚州為東揚州。

translations.literal: [9] On renchen day the commanderies of the capital region were made Yang Province, and Yang Province was renamed Eastern Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: [9] On renchen day the commanderies of the capital region were made Yang Province, and Yang Province was renamed Eastern Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以車騎將軍、揚州刺史豫章王子尚為司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi day Liu Zishang, Prince of Yuzhang, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yang Province, was made Minister over the Masses and Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Liu Zishang, Prince of Yuzhang, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yang Province, was appointed Minister over the Masses while retaining Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 去歲及是歲，東諸郡大旱，甚者米一升數百，京邑亦至百餘，餓死者十有六七。

translations.literal: In the previous year and in this year great drought struck the eastern commanderies; in the worst places a sheng of grain cost several hundred, and even in the capital it reached over a hundred; of those who starved, six or seven in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year and again this year the eastern commanderies suffered severe drought; in the worst-hit districts a sheng of grain cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital the price rose above a hundred; six or seven out of every ten people starved to death.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來，又立錢署鑄錢，百姓因此盜鑄，錢轉偽小，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian, moreover, mints had been established to cast coin, and because of this the common people illicitly cast as well; the money grew ever more counterfeit and small, and trade would not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiaojian era mints had also been set up to cast coin, which led the people to counterfeit it in turn; the currency grew ever smaller and more debased, and commerce ground to a halt.

sentences.zh: 永光元年春正月乙未朔，改元。

translations.literal: On yiwei day, the first of the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, the first of the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，省諸州臺傳。

translations.literal: On yisi day the provincial relay stations were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the provincial relay stations were abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以領軍將軍湘東王彧為衞將軍、南豫州刺史，護軍將軍建安王休仁為領軍將軍，祕書監山陽王休祐為豫州刺史，左衞將軍桂陽王休範為中護軍，南豫州刺史尋陽王子房為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army in chief, was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Protects the Army in chief; Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, General of the Left Guard, was made Central Army Guard; Liu Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, was made Inspector of Eastern Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, became chief General Who Protects the Army; Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, became Central Army Guard; and Liu Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, was transferred from Southern Yuzhou to Eastern Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，減州郡縣田祿之半。

translations.literal: On yichou day in the second month, the field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day in the second month, the field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties were cut in half.

sentences.zh: [10]庚寅，鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: [10] On gengyin day two-zhu coins were cast.
translations.idiomatic: [10] On gengyin day two-zhu coins were cast.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，罷臨江郡。

translations.literal: On jiachen day in the third month, Linjiang Commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day in the third month, Linjiang Commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，割郢州隨郡屬雍州。

translations.literal: On jihai day in the fifth month, Sui Commandery in Yingzhou was detached and placed under Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the fifth month, Sui Commandery in Yingzhou was transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以後軍司馬張牧為交州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu day Zhang Mu, Rear Army Major, was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Zhang Mu, Rear Army Major, was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，左軍長史劉道隆為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: On jisi day in the sixth month, Liu Daolong, Left Army Chief Clerk, was made Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day in the sixth month, Liu Daolong, Left Army Chief Clerk, was appointed Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，安西將軍、雍州刺史宗慤卒。

translations.literal: On yihai day Zong Que, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Zong Que, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，衞將軍、南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On renwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, was changed to Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, was reassigned as Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: [11]尚書令、驃騎大將軍柳元景加南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: [11] Liu Yuanjing, Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry, was given the additional post of Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Liu Yuanjing, Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry, was also made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛酉，越騎校尉戴法興有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: On xinyou day in the eighth month of autumn, Colonel of Fast Cavalry Dai Faxing was guilty of a crime and was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day in the eighth month of autumn, Colonel of Fast Cavalry Dai Faxing was found guilty of a crime and was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以尚書僕射顏師伯為尚書左僕射，[12]吏部尚書王景文為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On gengwu day Yan Shibo, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, [12] and Wang Jingwen, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Yan Shibo was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, [12] and Wang Jingwen, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝自率宿衞兵，誅太宰江夏王義恭、尚書令驃騎大將軍柳元景、尚書左僕射顏師伯、[13]廷尉劉德願。

translations.literal: On guiyou day the emperor himself led the palace guard troops and executed Grand Preceptor the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong; Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo; [13] and Director of Justice Liu Deyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the emperor personally led the palace guard and executed Grand Preceptor Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia; Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing; Left Vice Director Yan Shibo; [13] and Director of Justice Liu Deyuan.

sentences.zh: 改元為景和元年。

translations.literal: The reign title was changed to the first year of Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The reign title was changed to the first year of Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 文武賜位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks of advancement.

sentences.zh: 以領軍將軍建安王休仁為安西將軍、雍州刺史，衞將軍湘東王彧還為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Protects the Army in chief, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was restored as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was restored as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，司徒、揚州刺史豫章王子尚領尚書令，射聲校尉沈文秀為青州刺史，左軍司馬崔道固為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day Liu Zishang, Prince of Yuzhang, Minister over the Masses and Inspector of Yang Province, took on the concurrent post of Director of the Masters of Writing; Shen Wenxiu, Colonel of the Imperial Insignia Archers, was made Inspector of Qingzhou; Cui Daogu, Left Army Major, was made Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Liu Zishang, Prince of Yuzhang, Minister over the Masses and Inspector of Yang Province, also took charge of the Masters of Writing; Shen Wenxiu was appointed Inspector of Qingzhou; and Cui Daogu was appointed Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「昔凝神佇逸，磻溪讚道，湛慮思才，傅巖毗化。

translations.literal: On yihai day an edict declared: "In former times one concentrated the spirit and waited in stillness—at Panxi the Way was praised; one steeped the mind and thought of talent—at Fuyan they assisted in transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day an edict declared: "In former times rulers fixed their spirit in stillness—at Panxi the Way was praised; they steeped their minds in the search for talent—at Fuyan worthies aided the transformation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕位御三極，風澄萬宇，資鈇電斷，正卯斯戮。

translations.literal: I occupy the three extremities and the winds are clear throughout the myriad realms; with axe and lightning I cut off, and at the hour of mao the execution is carried out.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the three extremities and the winds are clear throughout the realm; with axe and lightning I have cut down the guilty, and at the hour of mao justice was done.

sentences.zh: 思所以仰宣遺烈，俯弘景祚，每結夢庖鼎，瞻言板築，有劬日昃，無忘昧旦。

translations.literal: I think how to look up and proclaim the legacy left behind, and look down to extend the bright fortune; night after night I dream of the cauldron in the kitchen, and when I speak of the plank road I do not forget the hour before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to look up and proclaim the legacy of my forebears and look down to extend the bright fortune of the throne; night after night I dream of the cauldron in the kitchen, and when I think of the plank road I do not forget the hour before dawn.

sentences.zh: 可甄訪郡國，招聘閭部：其有孝性忠節，幽居遯棲，信誠義行，廉正表俗，文敏博識，幹事治民，務加旌舉，隨才引擢。

translations.literal: Let the commanderies and kingdoms be searched and village districts recruited: those who have filial nature and loyal integrity, dwell in seclusion and shun the world, practice trustworthiness and righteous conduct, are pure and upright and set an example for custom, are refined in culture and broad in knowledge, or are capable in affairs and govern the people—all alike should be commended and, according to their talents, promoted and drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: Let every commandery and kingdom be searched and every district recruited: those of filial heart and loyal integrity, who dwell apart in seclusion, who practice trust and righteousness, who are pure and upright and set an example for others, who are cultured and learned, or who are capable in affairs and can govern the people—all should be commended and promoted according to their talents.

sentences.zh: 庶官克順，彝倫咸叙。

translations.literal: Thus officials will be able to conform and the human relations will all be set in order.
translations.idiomatic: Thus officials will perform their duties and the human order will be set right.

sentences.zh: 主者精加詳括，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Those in charge should examine this carefully in detail and report what accords with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge should examine each case carefully and report what accords with my intent.

sentences.zh: 」以始興公沈慶之為太尉，鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史王玄謨為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing, was made Grand Marshal; Wang Xuamo, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was made General Who Protects the Army in chief.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing, was appointed Grand Marshal; Wang Xuamo, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was made chief General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以石頭城為長樂宮，東府城為未央宮。

translations.literal: On gengchen day Stone City was made Changle Palace and the Eastern Palace quarter was made Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Stone City was renamed Changle Palace and the Eastern Palace quarter was renamed Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 罷東揚州并揚州。

translations.literal: Eastern Yang Province was abolished and merged into Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yang Province was abolished and merged back into Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以北邸為建章宮，南第為長楊宮。

translations.literal: On jiashen day the northern residence was made Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion was made Changyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day the northern residence was renamed Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion was renamed Changyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 以冠軍將軍邵陵王子元為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Ziyuan, Prince of Shaoling, General Who Conquers the Champions, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziyuan, Prince of Shaoling, General Who Conquers the Champions, was appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，原除吳、吳興、義興、晉陵、琅邪五郡大明八年以前逋租。

translations.literal: On bingxu day overdue rents before the eighth year of Daming in the five commanderies of Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langya were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day overdue rents before the eighth year of Daming in Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langya were remitted.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復立南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On jichou day the northern and southern imperial speedways were restored.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day the northern and southern imperial speedways were restored.

sentences.zh: 九月癸巳，車駕幸湖熟，奏鼓吹。

translations.literal: On guisi day in the ninth month the imperial carriage visited Hushu and imperial music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day in the ninth month the emperor visited Hushu, where imperial music was performed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On wuxu day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以南兗州刺史永嘉王子仁為南徐州刺史，丹陽尹始安王子真為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengzi day Liu Ziren, Prince of Yongjia, Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, was made Inspector of Southern Xuzhou; Liu Zizhen, Prince of Shi'an, Administrator of Danyang, was made Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Liu Ziren, Prince of Yongjia, was transferred from Southern Yanzhou to Southern Xuzhou; Liu Zizhen, Prince of Shi'an and Administrator of Danyang, was appointed Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞免為庶人，賜死。

translations.literal: On xinchou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was demoted to commoner status and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was stripped of rank and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以兗州刺史薛安都為平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu day Xue Andu, Inspector of Yanzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Xue Andu, Inspector of Yanzhou, was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，衞將軍湘東王彧加開府儀同三司，特進、右光祿大夫劉遵考為安西將軍、南豫州刺史，寧朔將軍殷孝祖為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingwei day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was given the additional title of Grand Master with the Golden Ax and Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes; Liu Zunkao, Special Advance and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Yin Xiaozu, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Dukes; Liu Zunkao was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; and Yin Xiaozu was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以前梁、南秦二州刺史柳元怙復為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: On wushen day Liu Yuangu, former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces, was restored as Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Liu Yuangu, former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces, was restored to that post.

sentences.zh: 己酉，車駕討征北將軍、徐州刺史義陽王昶，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On jiyou day the imperial carriage campaigned against Liu Chang, Prince of Yiyang, General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Xuzhou; the inner and outer courts were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day the emperor marched against Liu Chang, Prince of Yiyang, General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Xuzhou, and the court went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 昶奔于索虜。

translations.literal: Liu Chang fled to the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang fled to the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，右將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐進號鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: On xinhai day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General of the Right and Inspector of Yuzhou, was advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General of the Right and Inspector of Yuzhou, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以安西長史袁顗為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiayin day Yuan Yi, Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West, was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day Yuan Yi, Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West, was appointed Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以左民尚書劉思考為益州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Liu Kaokao, Director of the Left Household, was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Liu Kaokao, Director of the Left Household, was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 是日解嚴，車駕幸瓜步。

translations.literal: On that same day the alert was lifted and the imperial carriage visited Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the alert was lifted and the emperor went to Guabu.

sentences.zh: 開百姓鑄錢。

translations.literal: The common people were permitted to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Private coinage by the common people was permitted.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸亥，曲赦徐州。

translations.literal: On guihai day in the tenth month of winter, Xuzhou was granted a partial amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the tenth month of winter, Xuzhou was granted a partial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On bingyin day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, was appointed General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 己卯，東陽太守王藻下獄死。

translations.literal: On jimao day Wang Zao, Administrator of Dongyang, was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Wang Zao, Administrator of Dongyang, was thrown into prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 以宮人謝貴嬪為夫人，加虎賁靸戟，鸞輅龍旂，出警入蹕，實新蔡公主也。

translations.literal: The palace woman Xie Guibin was made Lady, with Tiger Guards bearing leather quivers and halberds, an imperial carriage with dragon banners, and imperial escort on going out and coming in; in truth she was Princess Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: The palace woman Xie Guibin was made Lady, granted Tiger Guards with leather quivers and halberds, an imperial carriage with dragon banners, and imperial escort whenever she went abroad—in truth she was Princess Xincai.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以鎮西大將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On yiyou day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and given the title of Grand Master with the Golden Ax and Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Dukes.

translations.literal: [14] (Editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: [14] (End of note.)

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，寧朔將軍何邁下獄死。

translations.literal: On renchen day in the eleventh month, He Mai, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day in the eleventh month, He Mai, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 新除太尉沈慶之薨。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi, newly appointed Grand Marshal, died.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, who had just been appointed Grand Marshal, died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，立皇后路氏，四廂奏樂。

translations.literal: On renyin day the Lady of the Lu clan was installed as empress, with music performed in all four side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Lady Lu was installed as empress, with music performed in all four side chambers of the palace.

sentences.zh: 赦揚、南徐二州。

translations.literal: Yang and Southern Xu provinces were granted an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was granted in Yang and Southern Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍建安王休仁加特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Protects the Army, was given the additional posts of Special Advance and Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Protects the Army, was also made Special Advance and Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 中護軍桂陽王休範遷職。

translations.literal: Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, Central Army Guard, was transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, Central Army Guard, was transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇子生，少府劉勝之子也。

translations.literal: On dingwei day a prince was born—the son of Liu Sheng of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day a prince was born, the son of Liu Sheng of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: [15]大赦天下。

translations.literal: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 贓汙淫盜，悉皆原除。

translations.literal: Corruption, defilement, licentiousness, and theft were all alike remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes of corruption, defilement, licentiousness, and theft were all remitted.

sentences.zh: 賜為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Those who had become heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had become heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以特進、左光祿大夫、護軍將軍建安王休仁為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On renzi day Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, Special Advance, Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and General Who Protects the Army, was made General of Agile Cavalry and given the title of Grand Master with the Golden Ax and Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先、安南侯敬淵並賜死。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Liu Jingyou, Prince of Nanping, Liu Jingxian, Prince of Luling, and Liu Jingyuan, Marquis of Annan, were all ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Liu Jingyou, Prince of Nanping, Liu Jingxian, Prince of Luling, and Liu Jingyuan, Marquis of Annan, were all ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 時帝凶悖日甚，誅殺相繼，內外百司，不保首領。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor's cruelty and perversity grew worse day by day; executions followed one after another, and within and without the hundred offices no one could be sure of keeping his head.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor's cruelty and perversity grew worse by the day; executions followed one after another, and throughout the bureaucracy no one could be sure of keeping his head.

sentences.zh: 先是訛言云：「湘中出天子。

translations.literal: Earlier a false rumor had spread, saying: "In Xiang a Son of Heaven will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rumor had spread: "A Son of Heaven will arise in Xiang.

sentences.zh: 」帝將南巡荊、湘二州以厭之。

translations.literal: " The emperor intended to tour Jing and Xiang provinces in the south to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang provinces to counter the omen.

sentences.zh: 先欲誅諸叔，然後發引。

translations.literal: He first wished to execute his uncles and only then set out on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to execute his uncles first and only then set out on the journey.

sentences.zh: 太宗與左右阮佃夫、王道隆、李道兒密結帝左右壽寂之、姜產之等十一人，謀共廢帝。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor secretly joined with his close attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er in plotting with eleven of the emperor's own attendants, including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chanzi, to depose the emperor together.
translations.idiomatic: The future Ming Emperor secretly allied with his close attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er and with eleven of the emperor's own attendants, including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chanzi, to depose him together.

sentences.zh: 戊午夜，帝於華林園竹林堂射鬼。

translations.literal: At midnight on wuwu day the emperor was at the Bamboo Grove Hall in Huilin Garden shooting at ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on wuwu day the emperor was in the Bamboo Grove Hall at Huilin Garden, shooting at ghosts.

sentences.zh: 時巫覡云：「此堂有鬼。

translations.literal: At that time shamans had said: "This hall harbors ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans had said that the hall was haunted:

sentences.zh: 」故帝自射之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the emperor shot at them himself.
translations.idiomatic: " so the emperor had gone to shoot at them himself.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之懷刀直入，姜產之為副。

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi, carrying a knife, went straight in, with Jiang Chanzi as his assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi entered with a drawn knife, Jiang Chanzi following as his second.

sentences.zh: 帝欲走，寂之追而殞之。

translations.literal: The emperor tried to flee; Jizhi pursued him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried to flee; Jizhi pursued him and struck him down.

sentences.zh: 時年十七。

translations.literal: He was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventeen years old.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令曰：

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order:
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order:

sentences.zh: 司徒領護軍八座：子業雖曰嫡長，少稟凶毒，不仁不孝，著自髫齔。

translations.literal: To the Minister over the Masses, chief General Who Protects the Army, and the Eight Dignitaries: Though Ziye was called the eldest son of the proper wife, from youth he received a vicious and poisonous nature; his lack of benevolence and filial piety were evident from his childhood locks.
translations.idiomatic: To the Minister over the Masses, the chief General Who Protects the Army, and the Eight Dignitaries: Though Ziye was the eldest son of the proper wife, from childhood he showed a vicious and poisonous nature; his want of benevolence and filial piety was evident even in his earliest years.

sentences.zh: 孝武棄世，屬當辰曆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiao Wu passed from the world, the throne fell to him by the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiao Wu died, the throne passed to him by right of succession.

sentences.zh: 自梓宮在殯，喜容靦然，天罰重離，歡恣滋甚。

translations.literal: From the time the imperial coffin lay in temporary lodging, his countenance was bright and calm; Heaven's punishment struck the li trigram, yet his wanton joy grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the imperial coffin lay in state, his face was bright and untroubled; though Heaven's punishment had struck the imperial house, his wanton joy only grew.

sentences.zh: 逼以內外維持，忍虐未露，而凶慘難抑，一旦肆禍，遂縱戮上宰，殄害輔臣。

translations.literal: Forced by inner and outer constraints to hold himself in check, his cruel and violent nature was not yet exposed; yet his savage brutality could not be restrained, and in a single day he unleashed disaster, wantonly slaughtering the chief ministers and annihilating his supporting officials.
translations.idiomatic: Forced by court and family to restrain himself, he had not yet shown his full cruelty; but his savage brutality could not be held back, and in a single day he unleashed catastrophe, slaughtering the chief ministers and destroying his own supporters.

sentences.zh: 子鸞兄弟，先帝鍾愛，含怨既往，枉加屠酷。

translations.literal: Ziluan and his brothers had been beloved of the late emperor; nursing old resentments, he wrongly subjected them to savage execution.
translations.idiomatic: Ziluan and his brothers had been the late emperor's favorites; nursing old resentments, he had them savagely executed without cause.

sentences.zh: 昶茂親作扞，橫相徵討。

translations.literal: Chang, a close kinsman, served as a bulwark, yet was wantonly attacked and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, a close kinsman who should have been a bulwark of the throne, was attacked and punished without cause.

sentences.zh: 新蔡公主逼離夫族，幽置深宮，詭云薨殞。

translations.literal: Princess Xincai was torn from her husband's clan and shut away in the deep palace; it was falsely announced that she had died.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xincai was torn from her husband's family and shut away in the inner palace, while a false report announced her death.

sentences.zh: 襄事甫爾，喪禮頓釋，昏酣長夜，庶事傾遺。

translations.literal: The mourning rites had barely begun when they were abruptly set aside; through long drunken nights every affair of state was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning had barely begun when its rites were cast aside; through long nights of drunkenness every affair of state was neglected.

sentences.zh: 朝賢舊勳，棄若遺土。

translations.literal: Court worthies and old ministers he cast off like discarded earth.
translations.idiomatic: Court worthies and old ministers he cast aside like rubbish.

sentences.zh: 管絃不輟，珍羞備膳。

translations.literal: Pipes and strings never ceased; rare delicacies filled every board.
translations.idiomatic: Music never ceased; rare delicacies filled every table.

sentences.zh: 詈辱祖考，以為戲謔。

translations.literal: He reviled and insulted his ancestors and forebears, making them the butt of his sport.
translations.idiomatic: He reviled his ancestors and forebears for sport.

sentences.zh: 行游莫止，淫縱無度。

translations.literal: His travels knew no stopping; his lewdness and excess had no measure.
translations.idiomatic: His wanderings knew no limit; his lewdness and excess knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 肆宴園陵，規圖發掘。

translations.literal: He held feasts in the imperial tombs and plotted to open the graves.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted in the imperial tombs and plotted to open the graves.

sentences.zh: 誅剪無辜，籍略婦女。

translations.literal: He executed and cut down the innocent and seized women by force.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered the innocent and seized women by force.

sentences.zh: 建樹偽豎，莫知誰息。

translations.literal: He raised false pillars, and no one knew whose turn would come next.
translations.idiomatic: He raised up false charges, and no one knew who would be struck down next.

sentences.zh: 拜嬪立后，慶過恒典。

translations.literal: In appointing concubines and installing an empress, his celebrations exceeded the constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In taking concubines and installing an empress, his celebrations exceeded all precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗室密戚，遇若婢僕，鞭捶陵曳，無復尊卑。

translations.literal: Kinsmen of the imperial clan and close relatives he treated like maidservants and slaves, beating and dragging them with no regard for rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinsmen and close relatives he treated like servants, beating and dragging them with no regard for rank.

sentences.zh: 南平一門，特鍾其酷。

translations.literal: The house of Nanping alone he singled out for especial cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Nanping alone he singled out for especial cruelty.

sentences.zh: 反天滅理，顯暴萬端。

translations.literal: He turned against Heaven and extinguished principle; his open violence had ten thousand faces.
translations.idiomatic: He turned against Heaven and extinguished moral principle; his open violence took ten thousand forms.

sentences.zh: 苛罰酷令，終無紀極，夏桀、殷辛，未足以譬。

translations.literal: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no limit; Xia Jie and Yin Xin would not suffice for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no limit; even Jie of Xia and Xin of Yin would not suffice for comparison.

sentences.zh: 闔朝業業，人不自保，百姓遑遑，手足靡厝。

translations.literal: Throughout the court everyone was in dread and no one could protect himself; the common people were in turmoil and did not know where to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the court everyone lived in dread and no one was safe; the people were in turmoil and did not know where to turn.

sentences.zh: 行穢禽獸，罪盈三千。

translations.literal: His conduct was filthier than a beast's; his crimes filled three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was more beastly than a beast's; his crimes were beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 高祖之業將泯，七廟之享幾絕。

translations.literal: The enterprise of the High Ancestor was on the verge of perishing; the offerings to the seven temples were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor's enterprise was on the verge of ruin; the offerings at the seven temples were nearly cut off.

sentences.zh: 吾老疾沈篤，每規禍鴆，憂煎漏刻，氣命無幾。

translations.literal: I am old and my illness deep and grave; each day I foresee the poisoned cup; my anxious torment drips with the clepsydra, and my breath and life will not long endure.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and gravely ill; each day I foresee the poisoned cup; anxiety consumes me with every drip of the water clock, and my life will not long endure.

sentences.zh: 開闢以降，所未嘗聞。

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age, such a thing has never been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Since the opening of the age, nothing like this has ever been heard of.

sentences.zh: 遠近思奮，十室而九。

translations.literal: Near and far alike yearn to rise up; nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far alike yearn to rise against him; nine houses in ten.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍湘東王體自太祖，天縱英聖，文皇鍾愛，寵冠列藩。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, is descended from the Great Ancestor; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity, and Emperor Wen cherished him—his favor surpassed all the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, is descended from the dynastic founder; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity, and Emperor Wen cherished him above all other princes.

sentences.zh: 吾早識神睿，特兼常禮。

translations.literal: I recognized his divine keenness early and treated him with especial courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: I recognized his keen intelligence early and treated him with especial honor.

sentences.zh: 潛運宏規，義士投袂，獨夫既殞，懸首白旗，社稷再興，宗祏永固，人鬼屬心，大命允集。

translations.literal: He secretly carried out a great design; men of righteousness rallied to him; the tyrant alone has now fallen, his severed head on the white banner; the altars of state are renewed, the ancestral temple secured forever; the hearts of men and ghosts alike turn to him, and the great mandate is duly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out his great design in secret; men of righteousness rallied to him; the tyrant has fallen, his severed head on the white banner; the altars of state are renewed and the ancestral temple secured; the hearts of men and spirits alike turn to him, and the great mandate is duly his.

sentences.zh: 且勳德高邈，大業攸歸，宜遵漢、晉，纂承皇極。

translations.literal: Moreover his merit and virtue are lofty and far-reaching; the great enterprise is his to receive; he should follow Han and Jin in ascending the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: His merit and virtue are lofty; the great enterprise is his to receive; let him follow the precedents of Han and Jin in ascending the throne.

sentences.zh: 主者詳舊典以時奉行。

translations.literal: Those in charge should examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge should examine the old statutes and carry them out without delay.

sentences.zh: 未亡人餘年不幸嬰此百艱，永尋情事，雖存若殞。

translations.literal: I, who have outlived my years, have unfortunately met this hundredfold calamity; forever revisiting these events, though I live I am as if dead.
translations.idiomatic: I, who have outlived my allotted years, have met this hundredfold calamity; whenever I revisit these events, though I live I am as one dead.

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 葬廢帝丹陽秣陵縣南郊壇西。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling County, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling County, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而狷急，在東宮每為世祖所責。

translations.literal: From childhood the emperor was impatient and harsh; in the Eastern Palace he was often rebuked by Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood the emperor was impatient and harsh; in the Eastern Palace he was often rebuked by his father.

sentences.zh: 世祖西巡，子業啟參承起居，書迹不謹，上詰讓之。

translations.literal: When Shizu toured the west, Ziye submitted memorials reporting on his daily comings and goings; his calligraphy was careless, and the emperor interrogated and reproved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiao Wu toured the west, Ziye submitted memorials on his daily routine; his calligraphy was careless, and the emperor rebuked him for it.

sentences.zh: 子業啟事陳謝，上又答曰：「書不長進，此是一條耳。

translations.literal: Ziye submitted a memorial apologizing, and the emperor again replied: "Your writing does not improve—this is one matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye submitted an apology, and the emperor replied again: "Your writing does not improve—that is one thing.

sentences.zh: 聞汝素都懈怠，狷戾日甚，何以頑固乃爾邪！

translations.literal: I hear you are by nature always lax and idle, and your perversity grows worse day by day—why are you so obstinately incorrigible!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear you are habitually lax and idle, and your perversity grows worse by the day—why are you so obstinately incorrigible!"

sentences.zh: 」初踐阼，受璽紱，悖然無哀容。

translations.literal: When he first took the throne and received the seal and ribbon, he was perverse and showed no grieving countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took the throne and received the imperial seal, he showed no grief at all.

sentences.zh: 始猶難諸大臣及戴法興等，既殺法興，諸大臣莫不震懾。

translations.literal: At first he still found the great ministers and Dai Faxing and others difficult to deal with; after he killed Faxing, none of the great ministers was not terrified.
translations.idiomatic: At first he still found the great ministers and Dai Faxing hard to control; after he killed Faxing, every great minister lived in terror.

sentences.zh: 於是又誅羣公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again executed the host of nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he executed the host of nobles.

sentences.zh: 元凱以下，皆被毆捶牽曳。

translations.literal: From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten and dragged about.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten and dragged about.

sentences.zh: 內外危懼，殿省騷然。

translations.literal: Within and without there was peril and dread; the palace halls were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court there was peril and dread; the palace halls were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 初太后疾篤，遣呼帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Empress Dowager's illness was critical, she sent for the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Empress Dowager's illness was critical, she sent for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「病人間多鬼，可畏，那可往。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sickrooms are full of ghosts—it is fearful; how could I go there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Sickrooms are full of ghosts—it is dreadful; how could I go there?"

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，語侍者：「將刀來，破我腹，那得生如此寧馨兒！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager grew angry and said to her attendants: "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a fine son!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager grew angry and told her attendants: "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a son!"

sentences.zh: 」及太后崩後數日，帝夢太后謂之曰：「汝不孝不仁，本無人君之相。

translations.literal: Several days after the Empress Dowager died, the emperor dreamed that the Empress Dowager said to him: "You are unfilial and unkind; by nature you have no aspect of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after the Empress Dowager died, the emperor dreamed that she said to him: "You are unfilial and unkind; you were never fit to be a ruler.

sentences.zh: 子尚愚悖如此，亦非運祚所及。

translations.literal: Zishang is foolish and perverse to this degree; he too is not what fortune and the throne can sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Zishang is as foolish and perverse as you; he too is not what fortune and the throne can sustain.

sentences.zh: 孝武險虐滅道，怨結人神，兒子雖多，並無天命。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao Wu was dangerous and cruel and extinguished the Way; his resentment bound men and spirits together; though his sons were many, none had Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiao Wu was cruel and extinguished the Way; his crimes bound men and spirits in resentment; though his sons were many, none had Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 大運所歸，應還文帝之子。

translations.literal: The great fortune turns where it belongs; it should return to a son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The great fortune turns where it belongs; it should return to a son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 」其後湘東王紹位，果文帝子也。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the Prince of Xiangdong succeeded to the throne, he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xiangdong later succeeded, he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 故帝聚諸叔京邑，慮在外為患。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing they would cause trouble if left abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing trouble if they remained in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 山陰公主淫恣過度，謂帝曰：「妾與陛下，雖男女有殊，俱託體先帝。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shanyin was licentious beyond measure; she said to the emperor: "Your Majesty and I, though man and woman differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shanyin was licentious beyond measure; she told the emperor: "Your Majesty and I, though man and woman differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下六宮萬數，而妾唯駙馬一人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ten thousand consorts in the six palaces, yet I have only one husband.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ten thousand women in the six palaces, yet I have only one husband.

sentences.zh: 事不均平，一何至此！

translations.literal: How unfair that matters should have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: How unfair that things should have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃為主置面首左右三十人；

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon set up thirty male favorites for the princess on her left and right;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon provided the princess with thirty male favorites;

sentences.zh: 進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王，食湯沐邑二千戶，[16]給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: her rank was advanced to Princess of Kuaiji Commandery, with precedence equal to a prince of a commandery, a fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance, [16] one set of imperial music, and twenty guards with ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: she was advanced to Princess of Kuaiji Commandery with precedence equal to a commandery prince, a fief of two thousand households, [16] one set of imperial music, and twenty guards with ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，與朝臣常共陪輦。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, he and the court ministers commonly accompanied the imperial carriage together.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out, court ministers commonly rode in the same carriage with him.

sentences.zh: 主以吏部郎褚淵貌美，就帝請以自侍，帝許之。

translations.literal: The princess, because Chu Yuan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was handsome in appearance, asked the emperor to let him serve her; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chu Yuan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was handsome, the princess asked the emperor to let him serve her, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 淵侍主十日，備見逼迫，誓死不回，遂得免。

translations.literal: Yuan served the princess for ten days, was pressed on all sides, and vowed he would rather die than submit; only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan served the princess for ten days, was pressed on every side, and swore he would rather die than submit; only then was he released.

sentences.zh: 帝所幸閹人華願兒，官至散騎常侍，加將軍帶郡。

translations.literal: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the emperor favored, reached the post of Attendant Cavalier and was made a general with a commandery attached.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the emperor favored, rose to Attendant Cavalier and was made a general with a commandery attached.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書，[17]頗識古事，自造世祖誄及雜篇章，往往有辭采。

translations.literal: From youth the emperor loved reading [17] and was quite versed in antiquity; he himself composed the eulogy for Shizu and various other pieces, which often had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor loved reading [17] and knew antiquity well; he composed the eulogy for his father and various other pieces that often showed real literary talent.

sentences.zh: 以魏武帝有發丘中郎將、摸金校尉，乃置此二官。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had had a General of Opening Mounds in the Middle and a Colonel of Touching Gold, he established these two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had had a General of Opening Mounds in the Middle and a Colonel of Touching Gold, he established the same two offices.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, and Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, were placed in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, and Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, were placed in charge of them.

sentences.zh: [18]其餘事迹，分見諸列傳。

translations.literal: [18] His other deeds are set forth separately in the various biographies.
translations.idiomatic: [18] His other deeds are set forth separately in the various biographies.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：廢帝之事行著于篇。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 若夫武王數殷紂之釁，不能絓其萬一；

translations.literal: When King Wu of Zhou counted the crimes of Zhou of Yin, he could not exhaust one part in ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Zhou counted the crimes of King Zhou of Yin, he could not exhaust one part in ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 霍光書昌邑之過，未足舉其毫釐。

translations.literal: when Huo Guang wrote out the faults of the Marquis of Haihun, he could not list one hair's breadth in a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: when Huo Guang set down the faults of the Marquis of Haihun, he could not list one hair's breadth in a thousand.

sentences.zh: 假以中才之君，有一于此，足以霣社殘宗，汚宮瀦廟，況總斯惡以萃一人之體乎！

translations.literal: Suppose an emperor of only middling talent had one of these faults— that alone would suffice to destroy the altars of state, ruin the ancestral temple, and defile the palace and shrine; how much more when all these evils are gathered in a single person's body!
translations.idiomatic: An emperor of only middling talent who committed one such fault would suffice to destroy the altars of state and defile the ancestral shrines; how much more when all these evils were gathered in a single body!

sentences.zh: 其得亡亦為幸矣。

translations.literal: That he escaped destruction was also a piece of good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That he perished when he did was itself a mercy.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 出居東宮 各本並脫「居」字，據元龜二五六補。

translations.literal: Moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace: All editions alike omit the character 「ju」; it is supplied according to Yuan Gui 256.
translations.idiomatic: 「Moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace」: all editions omit 「ju」; the character is restored from Yuan Gui 256.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史 「南豫」子仁傳作「南兗」。

translations.literal: Liu Ziren, Prince of Yongjia, Administrator of Danyang, was made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou: In Ziren's biography 「Southern Yuzhou」 appears as 「Southern Yanzhou」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Liu Ziren, Prince of Yongjia, Administrator of Danyang, was made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou」: Ziren's biography reads 「Southern Yanzhou」 instead.

sentences.zh: 繁而傷治 「傷」各本並作「作」，據元龜一九一改。

translations.literal: Burdensome and harmful to good government: In all editions 「harmful」 appears as 「make」; it is emended according to Yuan Gui 191.
translations.idiomatic: 「Burdensome and harmful to good government」: all editions read 「make」 for 「harmful」; emended per Yuan Gui 191.

sentences.zh: 氣緯舛互 「互」各本並作「玄」，蓋形近而譌，今改正。

translations.literal: The qi and celestial markers are at cross purposes: In all editions 「cross」 appears as 「mysterious」; this is likely a graphic confusion from similar forms, and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 「The qi and celestial markers are at cross purposes」: all editions read 「mysterious」 for 「cross」—likely a graphic confusion; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍青冀二州刺史 各本「鎮北將軍」下並衍「南徐州刺史新安王子鸞為」十一字。

translations.literal: General Who Protects the Army Wang Xuamo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces: Below 「General Who Pacifies the North」 all editions alike have the intrusive eleven characters 「Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, was made」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Wang Xuamo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji」: all editions insert eleven spurious characters after 「General Who Pacifies the North」.

sentences.zh: 按新安王子鸞傳，不言曾為青、冀二州刺史，而王玄謨傳，言玄謨時徙為青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, it is not stated that he ever served as Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, whereas Wang Xuamo's biography says that at this time Xuamo was transferred to be Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Ziluan's biography never makes him Inspector of Qing and Ji, while Xuamo's biography says he was transferred there at this time.

sentences.zh: 今訂正。

translations.literal: The text is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 己丑 各本並作「己未」。

translations.literal: Jichou day: In all editions this appears as 「jiwei」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Jichou day」: all editions read 「jiwei」.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，二十三日己丑，無己未、乙丑。

translations.literal: According to this, that month's dingmao was the first day; the twenty-third day was jichou—there was no jiwei or yichou.
translations.idiomatic: That month's dingmao was the first day; the twenty-third was jichou—neither jiwei nor yichou occurred.

sentences.zh: 今據建康實錄及通鑑改正。

translations.literal: It is now corrected according to the Veritable Records of Jiankang and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected per the Veritable Records of Jiankang and the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 庚寅 各本並作「庚子」。

translations.literal: Gengyin day: In all editions this appears as 「gengzi」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Gengyin day」: all editions read 「gengzi」.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，無庚子，二十三日己丑後，二十四日有庚寅。

translations.literal: According to this, that month's dingmao was the first day; there was no gengzi day. After the twenty-third day jichou, the twenty-fourth day was gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: That month's dingmao was the first day; there was no gengzi. The day after jichou (the twenty-third) was gengyin (the twenty-fourth).

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: It is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected here.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史 「宗越」書中多誤作「宋越」，今據宗越傳改正。

translations.literal: Zong Yue, General Who Assists the State, was made Inspector of Sizhou: 「Zong Yue」 is often wrongly written as 「Song Yue」 in the book; it is now corrected according to Zong Yue's biography.
translations.idiomatic: 「Zong Yue was made Inspector of Sizhou」: the book often miswrites his name as 「Song Yue」; corrected per his biography.

sentences.zh: 以下類此者皆逕改，不具校。

translations.literal: Similar cases below are all emended directly without separate collation.
translations.idiomatic: Similar cases below are emended directly without separate notes.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射 「尚書僕射」各本作「尚書左僕射」，南史無「左」字。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing: In all editions 「Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」 appears as 「Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」; the History of the Southern Dynasties has no 「Left」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」: all editions add 「Left」; the Southern History has none.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘宋書札記云：「左字衍，當據南史刪。

translations.literal: Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Song say: 「The character 「Left」 is intrusive and should be deleted according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Song: 「「Left」 is intrusive; delete it per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 」按是時但置尚書僕射，不分立左右。

translations.literal: 」According to this, at that time only Vice Directors of the Masters of Writing were appointed, with no separate left and right posts.
translations.idiomatic: 」At that time only a single Vice Director was appointed, with no left-right division.

sentences.zh: 今據南史刪「左」字。

translations.literal: 「Left」 is now deleted according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: 「Left」 is deleted per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 減州郡縣田祿之半 宋本、三朝本、北監本、毛本及南史作「田祿」。

translations.literal: The field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half: The Song edition, Three-Dynasties edition, Beijian edition, Mao edition, and Southern History read 「field stipends」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Field stipends … reduced by half」: the Song, Three-Dynasties, Beijian, and Mao editions and the Southern History read 「field stipends」.

sentences.zh: 殿本、局本作「田租」。

translations.literal: The Palace edition and Bureau edition read 「field rent」.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace and Bureau editions read 「field rent」.

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「祿秩」。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of Jiankang reads 「stipend ranks」.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of Jiankang reads 「stipend ranks」.

sentences.zh: 按普減國內田租之半，非封建統治者所肯為，此必減州郡縣官吏田祿之半。

translations.literal: According to this, a general halving of land rent throughout the realm is not something a feudal ruler would undertake; this must mean halving the field stipends of officials in provinces, commanderies, and counties by half.
translations.idiomatic: A general halving of land rent empire-wide is not something a feudal ruler would do; this must mean halving officials' field stipends in provinces, commanderies, and counties.

sentences.zh: 故建康實錄改稱為「祿秩」。

translations.literal: Therefore the Veritable Records of Jiankang changed the wording to 「stipend ranks」.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Veritable Records of Jiankang's wording 「stipend ranks」.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史 各本並脫「南」字。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, was changed to Inspector of Yongzhou: All editions alike omit the character 「Southern」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Liu Yu … Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, was changed to Inspector of Yongzhou」: all editions omit 「Southern」.

sentences.zh: 按明帝紀，永光元年為南豫州刺史，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the first year of Yongguang he was Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, garrisoning Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's annals show him as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, garrisoning Gushu, in Yongguang 1.

sentences.zh: 又按州郡志，此時南豫州鎮姑孰，而豫州則未嘗以姑孰為州治。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies, at this time Southern Yuzhou was garrisoned at Gushu, whereas Yuzhou had never had Gushu as its seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies shows Southern Yuzhou at Gushu, while Yuzhou never used Gushu as its seat.

sentences.zh: 今據明帝紀補。

translations.literal: 「Southern」 is now supplied according to the annals of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: 「Southern」 is restored per Emperor Ming's annals.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射顏師伯 「尚書左僕射」各本並作「尚書僕射」，據南史改，說見前。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing: In all editions 「Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」 appears as 「Vice Director of the Masters of Writing」; it is emended according to the Southern History, as explained above.
translations.idiomatic: 「Left Vice Director Yan Shibo」: all editions drop 「Left」; restored per the Southern History, as noted above.

sentences.zh: 以鎮西大將軍豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍開府儀同三司 鎮西大將軍各本並作「鎮北大將軍」。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and given the title equal to the Three Dukes: In all editions 「General Who Pacifies the West」 appears as 「General Who Pacifies the North」.
translations.idiomatic: 「General Who Pacifies the West … made General Who Pacifies the Army」: all editions read 「North」 for 「West」.

sentences.zh: 上九月辛亥下作鎮西大將軍，休祐傳亦作鎮西，今改正。

translations.literal: Above, under the ninth month on xinhai day, he is made General Who Pacifies the West; Xiuyou's biography also reads 「West」; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth-month xinhai entry and Xiuyou's biography both have 「West」; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 少府劉勝之子也 「劉勝」元龜一九七及二０七同本紀。

translations.literal: The son of Liu Sheng of the Palace Treasury: 「Liu Sheng」 appears in Yuan Gui 197 and 207 in the same annals.
translations.idiomatic: 「Son of Liu Sheng of the Palace Treasury」: Yuan Gui 197 and 207 agree with this annals.

sentences.zh: 符瑞志及始安王休仁傳、宋略、南史帝紀作劉矇，南史休仁傳作劉蒙。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Omens, the biography of Liu Xiuren, Prince of Shi'an, the Song Summary, and the imperial annals in the Southern History write 「Liu Meng」 with the character meng meaning "blind"; the biography of Liu Xiuren in the Southern History writes 「Liu Meng」 with the character meng meaning "cover".
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Omens, Xiuren's biography, the Song Summary, and the Southern History annals write the name as 「Liu Meng」 (blind); Xiuren's biography in the Southern History writes it as 「Liu Meng」 (cover).

sentences.zh: 食湯沐邑二千戶 「食」各本並作「侯」。

translations.literal: A fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance: In all editions 「receive」 appears as 「marquis」.
translations.idiomatic: 「Fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance」: all editions read 「marquis」 for 「receive」.

sentences.zh: 據御覽一五二改。

translations.literal: It is emended according to the Imperial Readings 152.
translations.idiomatic: Emended per the Imperial Readings 152.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書 「讀書」各本並作「講書」，據南史、元龜一九二、御覽一二八引改。

translations.literal: From youth the emperor loved reading: In all editions 「reading books」 appears as 「lecturing on books」; it is emended according to the Southern History, Yuan Gui 192, and the Imperial Readings 128 citation.
translations.idiomatic: 「From youth the emperor loved reading」: all editions read 「lecturing on books」; emended per the Southern History, Yuan Gui 192, and Imperial Readings 128.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁山陽王休祐領之 各本並脫「休仁山陽王」五字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, and Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, were placed in charge of them: All editions alike omit the five characters 「Xiuren, Prince of Shanyang」; they are supplied according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: 「Jian'an and Shanyang princes were placed in charge」: all editions omit 「Xiuren … Prince of Shanyang」; restored per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 張燴讀史舉正云：「按建安王乃休仁，休祐則山陽王也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hui's Corrections in Reading History says: 「According to this, the Prince of Jian'an is Xiuren, and Xiuyou is the Prince of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui's Corrections in Reading History: 「The Prince of Jian'an is Xiuren; Xiuyou is the Prince of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 南史作『以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之』為是。」

translations.literal: The Southern History's reading 「Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, and Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, were placed in charge of them」 is correct.」
translations.idiomatic: The Southern History's 「Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, and Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, were placed in charge of them」 is correct.」
